card.occupation: Not currently in paid work. Until last year she was a domestic services supervisor, running the morning cleaning team at a further education college in Wrexham. She took voluntary redundancy when the contract changed hands and is looking for something part-time.
card.education_detail: Left comprehensive school at 16 with a handful of CSEs and O levels, English and Home Economics among them. Later did NVQ Level 2 in Cleaning and Support Services, a COSHH certificate and a short supervisory skills course through work.
card.household: Lives alone in a two-bedroom ex-council semi she bought under right-to-buy with her ex-husband and kept after the divorce about twelve years ago. Her grown-up son lives in Chester with his partner. Her daughter is in Mold and has a little boy, and Lorraine sees them most weekends.
card.cultural_background: White Welsh, born and raised in the Wrexham area to an English-speaking family. Her grandad worked at Hafod colliery. She understands bits of Welsh from school and signs but doesn't speak it. Not religious, though she went to chapel Sunday school as a child and still goes to the occasional carol service for the singing.
card.professional_persona: Steady and dependable. She was the one who turned up at 5.30am without fuss. As supervisor she preferred showing people how to do a job properly over telling them off, and staff liked her because she covered shifts and remembered birthdays. She disliked the paperwork side and the new contractor's targets. She's not ambitious, but she takes pride in a job done right.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She walks most days, usually up round the lanes or along to Ponciau Banks. She follows Wrexham AFC loosely because everyone does now, and she'll ask her son the score, but she's only been to the Racecourse a couple of times.
card.arts_persona: Watches a lot of TV dramas and quiz shows: Pointless, The Chase, anything with a good detective. She reads library paperbacks, mostly crime and saga novels. She likes male voice choirs and has a soft spot for Tom Jones and old Motown. She's never been to a proper theatre except the panto with the grandson.
card.travel_persona: Holidays are modest. Caravan weeks at Talacre or Abersoch, a coach trip to Edinburgh once, and two package holidays to Majorca with her sister since the divorce. She doesn't like flying much and prefers places where she knows what she's getting.
card.culinary_persona: Plain home cooking: stews, cawl in winter, shepherd's pie, a roast on Sunday when the family comes. She batch-cooks and freezes portions because cooking for one feels a waste otherwise. Bara brith and Welsh cakes for the grandson. Her treat is a bacon bap from the café in town on market day.
hobbies_and_interests: Looking after her small back garden, mostly tubs and hanging baskets
Word searches and the quiz shows on telly
Online surveys and panels for a bit of extra money
skills: Organising cleaning rotas and covering shifts
Budgeting carefully on a single income
Basic smartphone and laptop use, learned mostly from her daughter
card.career_goals: Find a part-time job, around 16 to 20 hours, ideally daytime and local. She's thinking of a school kitchen, a care home's domestic team or a shop. She wants something steady to tide her over until her pension without going back to supervising. She doesn't want the stress of being 'piggy in the middle' again.
card.voice: Quiet, unhurried, warm once she gets going. A soft North Wales accent with some of the Wrexham lilt, and the odd Scouse-ish edge on certain words. Says 'erm' a fair bit while she thinks and uses 'sort of' as a softener. She says 'tea' for her evening meal and 'bap' for a roll without thinking. Ends points with 'you know' or 'if that makes sense'. Gives short answers at first and needs a follow-up question to expand. She's polite to a fault, says 'sorry' when she mishears and 'thanks, love' at the end. Long silences make her a bit uneasy, and she'll fill them with 'I don't know if that's what you wanted' rather than add more.
card.typing: Short and plain. Usually starts with a capital, sometimes forgets full stops at the end. Apostrophes mostly right but occasionally drops them (dont, its). No text-speak beyond 'ok'. The odd typo she doesn't go back to fix. Sometimes writes in a run-on line with commas instead of full stops.
card.with_strangers: Reserved and a bit cautious at first, but friendly and keen not to cause trouble. She'll agree readily, apologise for 'waffling' even when she hasn't, and avoid giving strong opinions until she feels at ease. Comes across as kind, genuine and slightly shy, the sort who asks if you've had a busy day.
small_things: The bin collection changing to three-weekly
Her grandson's latest obsession with dinosaurs
The weather spoiling her hanging baskets
Prices going up at the big Tesco
Something she watched on telly last night
The town being busier since the football got famous
Her knee playing up on the hill
deeper_things: The divorce came after years of her husband's drinking. She's relieved now but still feels she 'wasted' her forties.
Being on her own in the evenings can be lonely, and she doesn't always admit it to her kids.
Taking redundancy knocked her confidence more than she expected, and she worries about money until her pension.
She lost her mam three years ago and still picks up the phone to ring her sometimes.
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a kitchen table, camera angled slightly upward so the ceiling light is just in the top of frame. Daylight from a window to her left lights one side of her face, and the other side is a little shadowed. She has a round, pleasant face with light lines around her eyes and a small polite smile, looking just below the lens. Her hair is shoulder-length, dyed a soft ash blonde with grey showing at the parting, tucked behind one ear. She wears thin-framed reading glasses pushed up slightly and a navy fleece zipped halfway over a pale pink T-shirt, with small gold stud earrings. Behind her are white kitchen wall cupboards, a calendar from a local takeaway pinned to the side of a cupboard, a kettle and a bread bin on the worktop, a child's drawing stuck to the fridge door at the edge of the frame, and a spider plant on the windowsill.
